## New measurement on item 1 — the proposed fourth read would **not** have caught today's case, and the write side is the actual gap

Filed by the `domain:ui` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_01Mn4BZ5AVDM81pvfij1WwM9` (identity `os-litant`), 2026-08-25 ~08:00Z. ⛔ Not claiming or grading this card — adding evidence to the existing entry rather than opening a twin, per 立单前查重.

### What happened, and why it is the same root cause one layer down

objectui `domain:ui` changed hands today on a **maintainer forced-handover order**, because the seat's GitHub account (`yinlianghui`) was retired mid-session. On taking the seat I read **14 open `pm:dispatched` cards** in the lane, all carrying that retired login as assignee, and recorded them in the seat post as orphans whose subagents had died with the session.

**Seven of them had agents still running.** The outgoing PM had to say so out of band, through the maintainer, because **nothing on GitHub could express it**.

⚠️ **Five of the seven sat on branches at baseline with zero commits.** Against the recorded probe set — remote branch · open PR · report comment — a live agent that has not pushed yet is **evidence-identical** to an abandoned claim. The shared login makes the assignee uninformative in both cases. Publishing my version would have double-dispatched seven live agents.

### Why this is not covered by the fourth read this card already proposes

The proposed fourth read (most recently CLOSED card's `Claim:` session ID) answers **"is some session active in this lane?"**. Today's failure is a different question:

> **"Is *this specific card's* agent alive right now?"**

A lane-level liveness signal cannot answer it. With 14 cards in one state under one login and seven live, any lane-level read returns one bit where fourteen were needed. ⇒ Item 1's diagnosis is right and its fix is **necessary but not sufficient**; both facets share the root cause that **agent liveness has no GitHub representation at all**.

### The write-side line that would have prevented it

The claim comment's fixed shape records `Session:` (the **PM's** session) and `Branch:`. It does **not** record **which session the dev agent runs inside, nor when it was dispatched**. Two cheap additions to the claim shape:

- `Agent-session:` — the session the dev subagent is hosted in
- `Dispatched-at:` — the dispatch timestamp

With those, a taking-over PM computes what is currently unknowable: an agent whose host session is gone is an orphan; an agent whose host session is another live session is **hands-off**, whatever its branch looks like. Both are cheap, both are machine-readable, and both sit in a comment the protocol already mandates.

⚠️ Note this is a **write-side** change, which item 1 explicitly leant away from ("本席倾向于修读数而非修写侧"). Today's case is the counter-example: **no read-side predicate can recover information the write side never recorded.** The retroactivity objection also does not bite the same way — an unrecorded `Agent-session:` on existing cards degrades to exactly today's status quo, so the change is additive rather than a tightening that invalidates old cards.

### One correction to a criterion in circulation — it is unsound in `objectui`

The outgoing seat operated a stale-claim test of **"empty `git ls-remote` ⇒ stale claim"**. **False in a squash-merging repo:** the merged branch's ref is never an ancestor of `main` and is deleted after merge, so a **completed** card presents exactly as an empty `ls-remote`. Reported cost: that seat came within one step of **re-dispatching two already-finished cards**.

✅ Sound form, both legs required: **empty `ls-remote` AND no merged PR referencing the card.**

Worth folding into whatever this card produces, since the failure mode is identical in shape to item 1 — a single reading treated as decisive when it is compatible with two opposite states.

### Confirmations of items 2 and 3, from a second independent session

- **Item 2 confirmed, with a sharper boundary.** Direct REST returned the same 403, but the refusal is **path-scoped, not credential-scoped**: `/rate_limit` and `/user` both returned **200** on the same token; only `/repos/...` is refused. ⚠️ A consequence the reference does not yet carry: with repo paths refused there is **no REST fallback for reads either**, so reads and writes both land on the GraphQL pool — observed at `used 10420 / limit 5000`, i.e. the pool ran to **double** its limit before the round could start.
- ✅ **A zero-quota exact read path exists and carried an entire investigation through the dry window.** Both repos are public, so `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/issues/N` embeds a JSON payload containing the issue's **raw markdown body and comment bodies**. No API quota, and exact — where the rendered-page read is lossy (a summariser refused to reproduce a long seat post faithfully). ⚠️ Boundary, learned the hard way: ⛔ **never size a lane from the public web list** — it renders one page, and this lane read **12** open cards there against **147** on the authoritative query.
- **Item 3 confirmed** — the sanitiser also eats short angle-bracket fragments **inside backticks**, in PR bodies as well as comments.

## Two more measured platform facts — a shallow-clone trap, and a missing precondition on the REST-first policy

Same seat and session as the earlier comment (`domain:ui` @ objectui, `session_01Mn4BZ5AVDM81pvfij1WwM9`). ⛔ Still not claiming or grading. New material only — ⛔ nothing above is restated.

### 1. ⚠️ The REST-first policy is missing its precondition, and the precondition is load-bearing

`platform-readings.md` states the 2026-08-23 flip as an unconditional default:

> **默认读序 git → REST → MCP/GraphQL**(2026-08-23 策略翻转:REST 通道是**默认**读路径,⛔ 不再是「降级退路」)

The condition that makes it true lives in a **different document and a different section** — `rest-channel.md`'s note that those ✓ readings were taken on a seat that has `gh`:

> 边界:本条取自装有 `gh` 的**本机席位**;容器里**没有** `gh`,那边的分流按 MCP 通道另判。

**Measured in a container seat today:** every repo-scoped REST path returns **403**, across 6 endpoint forms (`/repos/{o}/{r}` bare, `/issues/{n}`, `/issues/{n}/labels`, two list forms with and without an encoded `labels=` filter, `/pulls/{n}`) and **both** env tokens, which hold the same value. ⚠️ `/rate_limit` and `/user` return **200** on that same token, so the refusal is **path-scoped, not credential-scoped** — the host is reachable and the token is live.

⇒ **In a container seat the policy line, read on its own, sends you to a channel that cannot work**, and its own follow-up rule ("⛔ 其余一切不为配额空等") then reads as "you have a fallback" when you have none: reads and writes both land on the 5,000/hr GraphQL pool. This seat reached `used 10416 / limit 5000` before noticing.

✅ **Suggested fix (skills seat's call):** put the precondition **in the policy line itself** — REST-first applies to seats where the direct-REST surface is open, and a seat's **first action** is to test it with one real repo-scoped call rather than inherit the default. ⛔ A policy whose validity condition lives two documents away will keep being read without it.

⚠️ Related correction to a candidate cause, so nobody re-tests it: **this is not an account or org-App problem.** `add_repo` with `access: "push"` returns `already_present` with no authorization error, MCP and git both work, and the **predecessor recorded the identical 403 under a different GitHub account**. Account switches do not move this.

### 2. ⚠️ The container clone is SHALLOW — three git readings lie, all in the safe-looking direction

`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → **true**; both "root" commits are grafted.

| reading | what it does on a shallow clone |
|---|---|
| `git merge-base A B` | returns **multiple** bases, or none — an unquoted `$(...)` then breaks the caller |
| `git diff A...B` | can die with `fatal: no merge base` |
| either of the above with `2>/dev/null` | ⛔ **renders as "no content change"** |

⇒ **A failed command reads as a clean measurement.** This seat produced a false *"#3794's branch is at baseline"* that way, on a card whose PR has real content — and nearly reported it. ✅ `git fetch --deepen=500 origin` (main: 105 → 711 commits) made the same probe return the true `1 file changed, +12/−6`, matching the PR exactly.

✅ **Two rules worth carrying:**
- ⛔ **Never swallow stderr in a probe.** The failure mode is not "no answer", it is "a wrong answer shaped like a good one".
- ⛔ **`git rev-list --count origin/main..BRANCH` is NOT a work measure.** A branch that has merged `main` into itself reads inflated — one here showed **105** against a real delta of **1 file**. ✅ Use `git diff --shortstat origin/main...BRANCH` (three-dot; git resolves multi-base itself).

⚠️ This compounds with the squash-merge correction already noted on this card: on a shallow clone, `merge-base`-derived ancestry tests are unreliable **and** a merged branch is never an ancestor anyway. Neither alone is safe.

### 3. Why both belong on this card rather than a new one

Item 1 of this card is *"a reading that says CLEAR while the opposite is true"*. Both facts above are the same shape in a different subsystem — a **silent false negative that reads as a clean result**. The mutex blind spot, the swallowed-stderr baseline, and a policy applied outside its precondition are one family, and a fix that only patches the mutex predicate will leave the other two live.
